title: What operations management is
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No existing point teaches what operations management is; the systems approach mentions inputs becoming outputs, but it is a management theory, not the operations function and its role in cost and quality.

draft.title: What operations management is
card: Operations is the part of a business that turns inputs into the goods or services it sells. Inputs are the resources put in, such as materials, labour, equipment and information.
The finished goods or services are the outputs. A bakery turns flour, staff time and ovens into bread.
Operations management is the planning and control of this process, so that outputs are made well and on time.
Managing operations well can lower costs, for example by cutting waste. It can also lift quality, so the output suits what customers want.
draft.remember: Operations management plans and controls how inputs become outputs, aiming for lower costs and higher quality.

a.q: Which of these is the best example of operations turning inputs into outputs?
opts: A joinery uses timber and workers to build tables
A joinery runs an online advertising campaign
A joinery borrows money to buy a new van
A joinery hires a new accountant to check its books
a.why: Operations turns inputs such as timber and labour into the goods sold, which are the tables. The advertising campaign is an attempt to attract customers and does not make the product.
a.clue: Look for the option where resources become something sold.

b.q: Priya runs a laundry in Geelong. She changes how clothes move between machines, so less time and power are wasted and fewer items need rewashing. What is the most likely result?
opts: Lower costs and better quality of service
Lower costs but poorer quality of service
Higher costs but better quality of service
Higher outputs but more inputs per item
b.why: Better planning and control of the process cuts waste, which lowers costs. Fewer rewashes also means the service is of better quality. Lower cost does not have to mean lower quality, as waste can be cut without harming the output.
b.clue: Less waste and fewer rewashes affect both cost and quality.

a.best: A joinery uses timber and workers to build tables

b.best: Lower costs and better quality of service
